record.paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Given a morphism f and a letter a such that a is the initial letter of f (a), is it decidable that f ω (a) is quasiperiodic?

evidence.quote: Given a morphism f and a letter a such that a is the initial letter of f (a), is it decidable that f ω (a) is quasiperiodic?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a finite alphabet and $A^*$ (resp. $A^\omega$) the set of finite (resp. one-sided infinite) words over $A$. A finite word $q \in A^+$ is said to be a quasiperiod of a (finite or infinite) word $w$ if every position of $w$ lies inside an occurrence of $q$ in $w$; that is, $w$ can be covered by (possibly overlapping) occurrences of $q$. An infinite word $w \in A^\omega$ is called quasiperiodic if it admits at least one quasiperiod.

A morphism is a map $f: A^* \to A^*$ extended to words by concatenation. A letter $a \in A$ is said to be prolongable for $f$ if $a$ is the first letter of $f(a)$ and $|f^n(a)| \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$; in this case the iteration produces a unique infinite fixed point
$$f^\omega(a) = \lim_{n \to \infty} f^n(a) \in A^\omega.$$

Question: Is there an algorithm which, given as input a finite alphabet $A$, a morphism $f: A^* \to A^*$, and a letter $a \in A$ that is the initial letter of $f(a)$ (with $f$ prolongable on $a$), decides whether the infinite word $f^\omega(a)$ is quasiperiodic?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches surface methods for computing the set of quasiperiods of morphic words and characterizations of quasiperiodicity in special families (e.g. Sturmian morphic words by Lévé–Richomme), as well as related decidability results for ultimate periodicity of morphic words. However, no source explicitly announces a decision procedure for quasiperiodicity of an arbitrary morphic word $f^\omega(a)$, nor an undecidability result. The status therefore appears to remain unresolved based on accessible sources.

status_evidence.title: Quasiperiodic Sturmian words and morphisms
status_evidence.snippet: Characterization of quasiperiodicity for the restricted class of Sturmian morphic words.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist for special subclasses (Sturmian), suggesting the general decidability question is not settled.

status_evidence.title: Quasiperiodic infinite words: multi-scale case and dynamical properties
status_evidence.snippet: A method to determine the set of quasiperiods of an arbitrary infinite word, especially well-suited for morphic words.
status_evidence.claim: Methods exist for analyzing quasiperiods of morphic words but no explicit decision algorithm for general morphic quasiperiodicity is claimed.

status_evidence.title: On the Periodicity of Morphic Words
status_evidence.snippet: Decidability of ultimate periodicity for morphic words.
status_evidence.claim: Related periodicity decision problems for morphic words have been resolved, but quasiperiodicity is a different and apparently still-open question.
